commands: /bin/bash -lc "sed -n '1,180p' scripts/wf_run.py; sed -n '360,420p' scripts/wf_run.py; sed -n '540,610p' app/workspace.py; sed -n '3110,3285p' app/mcp_stdio.py"
final_text:
CAUSE: Identical calls get distinct workflow call keys, but their workspace names discard the part that distinguishes them.

Evidence: `WorkflowEngine._call_key()` hashes the canonical call payload and appends an occurrence number, producing keys like `<same SHA-256>:0`, `:1`, and `:2`. In `_run_attempt()`, `name` uses only `call_key[:12]`, so all three calls get the same worktree name for the same attempt. At concurrency 3, `app.workspace.create_worktree()` serializes creation under `repo_mutation_lock`; after the first creates that path, the next raises `ValueError("worktree already exists")`. Different prompts usually have different hash prefixes, so their names differ.

Recommended fix: include the occurrence component in the worktree name (or another unique per-call identifier), while keeping names within Git’s branch and filesystem limits. The path must uniquely identify each full `call_key` and attempt.
